items.title: Section: Light Affliction Closes; Approaching a Fruit Opens the Four Stages

items.zh: 云何薄塵性補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，先餘生中，於貪煩惱不修、不習、不多修習，已能於彼多見過患，已能厭壞、已善推求。由是因緣，今此生中，於所愛事會遇現前，眾多美妙上品境中，起微劣貪；於其中品、下品境中，貪全不起。如貪、瞋、癡、慢、尋思應知亦爾。是名薄塵性補特伽羅。云何行向補特伽羅？謂行四向補特伽羅。何等為四？一、預流果向，二、一來果向，三、不還果向，四、阿羅漢果向。是名行向補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a practitioner of light affliction? It is one who, in previous lives, did not cultivate desire, but had already come to see its many dangers, developed genuine revulsion towards it, and skilfully investigated it. Through this cause, in the present life, when encountering even the most excellent and appealing objects, only the faintest, most minor desire arises — and towards middling or inferior objects, no desire arises at all. The same holds for aversion, delusion, pride, and discursive thought. This is called a practitioner of light affliction. What is a practitioner approaching a fruit? It is one practising towards one of the four fruits. What are the four? Approaching the fruit of stream-entry, approaching the fruit of once-returning, approaching the fruit of non-returning, and approaching the fruit of arhatship. This is called a practitioner approaching a fruit.

items.title: Abiding in a Fruit: The Four Attainments Themselves

items.zh: 云何住果補特伽羅？謂住四果補特伽羅。何等為四？一、預流果，二、一來果，三、不還果，四、阿羅漢果。是名住果補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a practitioner abiding in a fruit? It is one abiding in one of the four fruits. What are the four? The fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship. This is called a practitioner abiding in a fruit.

items.title: Section: Faith-Followers and Dharma-Followers, Renamed Upon Touching the Fruit

items.zh: 云何隨信行補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，從他求請教授教誡，由此力故，修證果行。非如所聞、所受、所究竟、所思、所量、所觀察法，自有功能、自有勢力隨法修行；唯由隨他補特伽羅，信而修行。是名隨信行補特伽羅。云何隨法行補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，如其所聞、所受、所究竟、所思、所量、所觀察法，自有功能、自有勢力隨法修行；不從他求教授教誡，修證果行。是名隨法行補特伽羅。云何信勝解補特伽羅？謂即隨信行補特伽羅，因他教授教誡，於沙門果得觸證時，名信勝解補特伽羅。云何見至補特伽羅？謂即隨法行補特伽羅，於沙門果得觸證時，說名見至補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a faith-follower? It is one who seeks instruction and guidance from another, and, through that power, cultivates and realises the fruit. … Relying solely on another, such a one practices through faith. This is called a faith-follower. What is a dharma-follower? It is one who, through what has been heard, received, thoroughly understood, reflected upon, weighed, and observed, has their own capability and their own strength to practise in accordance with the teaching, not seeking instruction and guidance from another. This is called a dharma-follower. What is one liberated through resolute faith? It is precisely the faith-follower who, through another's instruction and guidance, upon touching the fruit of renunciation, is called one liberated through resolute faith. What is one who has reached right view? It is precisely the dharma-follower who, upon touching the fruit of renunciation, is called one who has reached right view.

items.title: The Body-Witness: Mastery of the Eight Liberations

items.zh: 云何身證補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，於八解脫順逆入出身作證，多安住，而未能得諸漏永盡。是名身證補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a body-witness? It is one who has personally realised, and dwells extensively within, the eight liberations, entering and emerging from them in forward and reverse order, yet who has not yet permanently exhausted every outflow. This is called a body-witness.

items.title: Section: Bound for at Most Seven More Rebirths — The Classic Stream-Enterer

items.zh: 云何名為極七返有補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，已能永斷薩迦耶見、戒禁取、疑三種結故，得預流果，成無墮法，定趣菩提。極七返有天人往來。極至七返，證苦邊際。如是名為極七返有補特伽羅。
items.en: What is meant by one bound for at most seven more rebirths? It is one who has permanently severed the three fetters — self-view, attachment to wrong rules and rituals, and doubt — thereby attaining the fruit of stream-entry, becoming incapable of falling into a lower rebirth, and certain to reach awakening. … Bound for at most seven more rebirths between the heavens and the human world, such a one reaches the very limit of suffering. This is called one bound for at most seven more rebirths.

items.title: Family-to-Family: A Stream-Enterer Advancing Towards the Second Fruit

items.zh: 云何家家補特伽羅？謂有二種家家。一、天家家，二、人家家。天家家者，謂於天上，從家至家，若往、若來，證苦邊際。人家家者，謂於人間，從家至家，若往、若來，證苦邊際。當知此二，俱是預流補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a family-to-family practitioner? There are two kinds: the heavenly family-to-family, and the human family-to-family. The heavenly family-to-family is one who, passing from family to family in the heavens, going and coming, reaches the very limit of suffering there. The human family-to-family is one who, passing from family to family in the human world, going and coming, reaches the very limit of suffering there. Know that both of these are, in terms of fruit, still stream-enterers.

items.title: Section: One Interval Remaining, and Three Sparks of Nirvana in the Between-State

items.zh: 云何一間補特伽羅？謂即一來補特伽羅，行不還果向，已能永斷欲界煩惱上品、中品，唯餘下品。唯更受一欲界天有，即於彼處得般涅槃，不復還來生此世間。是名一間補特伽羅。云何中般涅槃補特伽羅？謂有三種中般涅槃補特伽羅。一、有一種中般涅槃補特伽羅，從此沒已，中有續生；中有生已，便般涅槃。如小札火，微星纔舉，即便謝滅。二、有一種中般涅槃補特伽羅，從此沒已，中有續生；中有生已，少時經停，未趣生有，便般涅槃。如鐵摶鋌，炎熾赫然，鎚鍛星流，未下便滅。三、有一種中般涅槃補特伽羅，從此沒已，中有續生；中有生已，往趣生有，未得生有，便般涅槃。如彼熱鐵，椎鍛星流，下未至地，即便謝滅。如是三種中般涅槃補特伽羅，總說為一中般涅槃補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a practitioner with one interval remaining? It is precisely the once-returner, now approaching non-returning, who has permanently eliminated the upper and middle grades of desire-realm affliction, leaving only the lower grade — needing only one further rebirth among the gods of the desire realm, attaining final nirvana there, never again returning to be reborn in this world. This is called one with one interval remaining. What is a practitioner attaining final nirvana in the intermediate state? There are three kinds. … One such practitioner, having just died here, no sooner has the intermediate-state body arisen than final nirvana occurs — like a tiny fire of wood shavings, whose faint spark is extinguished the very instant it appears. … A second, having remained briefly in the intermediate state, attains final nirvana before proceeding towards rebirth — like sparks flying from hammered iron glowing in the fire, vanishing before they fall. … A third, having proceeded towards rebirth but not yet arrived at it, attains final nirvana then — like those same sparks from the hammered iron, vanishing just before they reach the ground. These three kinds together are called, as one, a practitioner attaining final nirvana in the intermediate state.

blocks.text: The noble persons of early Buddhism, as the treatise classifies them. These terms recur throughout Buddhist literature.

One of **light affliction** has in previous lives already seen desire's dangers; now even before the most attractive objects "only the faintest desire arises". Those **approaching a fruit** are on the way to stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, or arhatship. Venerable Miào Jìng: "approaching stream-entry" is widened to include the stages of heat, summit, patience, and highest worldly dharma.
One of the four fruits: stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, arhatship.

A **faith-follower** "seeks instruction and guidance from another, and through that power cultivates the fruit". A **Dharma-follower** relies on their own understanding of the teaching. On attaining the fruit they are renamed: **resolved by faith** and **arrived at right view**. Venerable Miào Jìng: instruction is Dharma; guidance is Vinaya.

One who "has personally realised, and dwells extensively within, the eight liberations", but has not yet exhausted the corruptions. Master Cháng Bǎi: "body" here means the mind-body, realisation in person.

One who has cut the three fetters (self-view, attachment to rules and rituals, and doubt) has attained stream-entry, and will be reborn at most seven times among gods and humans. Venerable Miào Jìng: such a one cannot fall into the lower realms.

subs.head: Family to family; one interval; between-states

blocks.text: A stream-enterer advancing towards the second fruit passes "from family to family" in heavens or among humans. The **one-interval** has cut most of the desire-realm afflictions, with only one rebirth left. Some non-returners attain final nirvāṇa in the intermediate state: three kinds, compared to sparks flying from struck iron.

quiz.q: How does a practitioner of light affliction react to excellent objects, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say "dust" means?
options: only faint desire, none for middling or lesser objects; "dust" means affliction
quiz.why: "When encountering even the most excellent and appealing objects, only the faintest, most minor desire arises — and towards middling or inferior objects, no desire arises at all." Master Cháng Bǎi: "dust" means affliction; the practitioner of light dust has very light afflictions.

quiz.q: According to Venerable Miào Jìng, how does the Satyasiddhi widen "approaching stream-entry"?
options: widened to include heat, summit, patience, and highest worldly dharma
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: it widened "approaching stream-entry" to include heat, summit, patience, and highest worldly dharma — unlike the Sarvāstivāda, which limits it to the path of seeing.

quiz.q: The faith-follower seeks instruction and guidance from others. How do the masters distinguish the two?
options: Miào Jìng: instruction is Dharma, guidance is Vinaya; Cháng Bǎi: instruction concerns concentration and wisdom, guidance the precepts
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: instruction is Dharma, guidance is Vinaya — Dharma and discipline, by which the path is accomplished. Master Cháng Bǎi: such beings seek instruction in concentration and wisdom, and guidance in the precepts.

quiz.q: How do the masters read "body" in "realising with the body"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the mind-body — the sixth consciousness, "body" meaning accumulation; Miào Jìng: "body" means mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: why "realise with the body"? Body means the mind-body — the sixth consciousness — "body" in the sense of accumulation. Venerable Miào Jìng: this "body" refers to the mind, which realises the quiescent nature of phenomena.

quiz.q: Which three fetters has the seven-rebirth practitioner severed, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say each obstructs?
options: self-view, attachment to rules and rituals, doubt; obstructing the emptiness, wishless, and signless concentrations
pride, doubt, views; the three wisdoms
quiz.why: "One who has permanently severed the three fetters — self-view, attachment to wrong rules and rituals, and doubt." Master Cháng Bǎi: self-view most closely obstructs the emptiness concentration; attachment to rules, the wishless; doubt, the signless.

quiz.q: By fruit, what are the heavenly and human family-to-family practitioners, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say they are by the four approaches?
options: both stream-enterers; with three conditions met they are renamed family-to-family, which by the approaches is approaching the second fruit
quiz.why: "Know that both of these are, in terms of fruit, still stream-enterers." Master Cháng Bǎi: when three conditions are met they are renamed family-to-family; in terms of the four approaches, they belong to the approach to the second fruit.

quiz.q: What is the "intermediate" in nirvāṇa in the intermediate state, as Master Cháng Bǎi defines it?
options: the intermediate state, or between-existence — the consciousness-body after death and before rebirth
quiz.why: "What is a practitioner attaining final nirvana in the intermediate state? There are three kinds." Master Cháng Bǎi: "intermediate" is the between-state, also called intermediate existence — the consciousness-body after death and before rebirth.
